content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

I've drafted the baseline specification. **This is the spec review gate** — per our Spec-Driven Development workflow, nothing gets planned or built until you approve this. Please review.

---

## 📄 Specification: Bookmark Manager

**Location:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`

### What the app does (user stories, in priority order)

1. **Save a bookmark (P1 — the MVP)** — Paste a web address; the app saves it with a title (auto-derived if you don't give one) and optional tags. Invalid/empty addresses are rejected with a clear message.
2. **Browse & find (P2)** — See all saved bookmarks; search/filter by keyword across title, address, and tags, with a clear "no matches" state.
3. **Organise, edit & remove (P3)** — Edit titles and tags, filter by tag, and delete bookmarks (with a confirmation step).

### Notable behaviours
- Warns on duplicate addresses
- Friendly empty state when nothing is saved
- Delete requires confirmation

### Success criteria (measurable)
- Save a bookmark in under 20s; find one among 100 in under 10s; 100% persistence across restarts; 90% of first-timers succeed unaided.

### Scope boundaries for v1 (assumptions — please confirm)
These are the calls I made where your request was open-ended. Flag any you disagree with:

| # | Assumption |
|---|-----------|
| 1 | **Single-user personal app** — no sign-in/accounts/sharing |
| 2 | **Web app** accessed through a browser |
| 3 | **Local storage only** — no cross-device sync or cloud backup |
| 4 | Stores the **reference + title only** — does not archive full page contents |
| 5 | **No browser import/export** in v1 |

---

**Does this match what you had in mind?**

- ✅ If it looks right, say so and I'll proceed to the **plan** gate (`speckit-plan`).
- ✏️ If anything's off — especially the scope assumptions above — tell me and I'll revise the spec before we move on.

I will **not** start planning or writing code until you approve.

This isn’t ready for approval yet. The single-user browser app is right, and I don’t need accounts, sharing, or cross-device syncing in this version. However, several important parts of managing bookmarks are missing or too limited:

- When I save a link, I expect the app to collect the page title, description, icon, and preview image automatically. I should be able to change the title and description both before and after saving.
- Saving the same address again should not merely warn me; it should take me to the existing bookmark so I can edit it, without creating a duplicate.
- I need to edit the address, title, description, tags, and a longer note. Notes should support basic formatting and display that formatting when viewed.
- The main list should show the title, description, tags, and page icon, and selecting a bookmark should open the original page.
- Search should ignore letter case and cover titles, descriptions, notes, and addresses. I also want tag searches such as `#travel`, exact phrases in quotation marks, and combinations using AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.
- When entering tags, I’d like suggestions from tags I have already used.
- I need a “read later” state, with a separate unread view and a way to mark items read.
- I need archiving as well as deletion. Archived bookmarks should disappear from the normal list and search, appear in a separate archive view, and be restorable.
- I want to select multiple bookmarks and change their tags, read status, archive status, or delete them together. I should also be able to apply those actions to everything matching my current search or filter.
- The list needs sorting, such as by date added or title.
- I want to save useful combinations of searches and included or excluded tags for reuse.
- I do want import and export using the usual browser bookmark file format, preserving titles, tags, and dates.
- I want the app to preserve a local copy of a page, with PDFs saved as PDFs, and optionally save a copy through the Internet Archive.
- I’d also like personal display choices such as the default sorting, how many items are shown, and text size.

So assumptions 4 and 5 need changing: this should preserve more than just the address and title, and import/export should be included. Please revise the specification and give the affected behaviours clear acceptance examples before we move to planning.

content:
The spec is revised. Everything you raised is now captured in the specification (not patched into code). Here's what changed.

---

## 📄 Specification revised: Bookmark Manager (review 1)

**Location:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`

### Assumptions 4 & 5 — now reversed as you asked
- **4 (was "reference + title only")** → the app now preserves rich metadata (title, description, icon, preview image), formatted notes, and **local page copies (PDFs as PDFs) plus optional Internet Archive** saving.
- **5 (was "no import/export")** → **import/export in the standard browser bookmark file format**, preserving titles, tags, and dates, is now in scope.

### The spec now has 12 prioritised user stories
| Story | Priority | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Save with auto metadata | P1 | title/description/icon/preview auto-collected; editable before & after |
| 2 Re-save opens existing | P1 | no duplicates — opens the existing bookmark for editing |
| 3 Browse, sort, open | P1 | list shows title/description/tags/icon; sort by date/title; opens original |
| 4 Powerful search | P2 | case-insensitive over title/description/note/address; `#tag`, "phrases", AND/OR/NOT/parens |
| 5 Rich editing + notes | P2 | edit address/title/description/tags/note; formatted notes; tag suggestions |
| 6 Read-later | P2 | unread state, dedicated unread view, mark read |
| 7 Archive & delete | P2 | archive hides from list/search + restorable; delete needs confirmation |
| 8 Bulk actions | P3 | multi-select or "all matching"; tags/read/archive/delete |
| 9 Saved searches | P3 | named query + included/excluded tag sets |
| 10 Import/export | P3 | browser bookmark format, preserving titles/tags/dates |
| 11 Local preservation + Internet Archive | P3 | offline copy, PDFs as PDFs, optional web archive |
| 12 Display preferences | P3 | default sort, items per view, text size |

Each affected behaviour has **Given/When/Then acceptance scenarios** (e.g. story 4 includes `#travel AND (japan OR korea) NOT flight` and a malformed-query case; story 2 handles trailing-slash/host-case duplicates; story 11 handles preservation failure). Edge cases, 29 functional requirements (FR-001–029), key entities, and 7 measurable success criteria are all updated.

### Three defaults I chose — please confirm or correct
These filled genuine gaps in your feedback; they're recorded in **Assumptions**:

1. **New bookmarks default to *unread*** — so the read-later view is useful immediately.
2. **"Basic formatting" for notes** = bold, italic, lists, links (unsupported formatting dropped safely).
3. **"Standard browser bookmark format"** = the common HTML *Netscape bookmark* file, carrying tags/dates via its conventional attributes.

---

**Next step:** review the full spec at `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`.

- ✅ Approve (and confirm/adjust the 3 defaults above) → I proceed to the **plan** gate.
- ✏️ More changes → I'll revise the spec again first.

I won't start planning or code until you approve.

This is very close, but I’d like a few details corrected before I approve it:

- New bookmarks should not all become unread automatically. They should be ordinary bookmarks unless I choose “read later” while saving or mark them unread afterward.
- A preserved web page should be stored as a self-contained HTML file. A PDF should remain a PDF.
- Bulk tag changes need to let me explicitly add or remove tags without unintentionally replacing a bookmark’s other tags.
- Please make the search rules explicit: a tag term and an ordinary text term together should both have to match, and the words AND, OR, or NOT should be treated as ordinary search text only when I put them in quotation marks.

The proposed basic note formatting and the Netscape HTML import/export format are both fine. Once those corrections are included, I’m happy to approve the specification.

All four corrections are in the spec at `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`.

---

## ✅ Corrections applied (review 2)

1. **Read-later default** — new bookmarks are now **ordinary (read)** by default; they become unread only if you pick "read later" while saving or mark them unread later.
   - Story 6 scenarios 3–4, **FR-016**, and Assumptions updated.

2. **Preserved copy format** — a web page is stored as a **single self-contained HTML file**; a PDF stays a **PDF**.
   - Story 11 intro + scenario 1, **FR-024**, Key Entities, and Assumptions updated.

3. **Bulk tag changes** — now explicitly **add or remove specific tags without replacing** a bookmark's other tags.
   - Story 8 scenario 1a and **FR-019** updated.

4. **Explicit search rules** — added:
   - Adjacent terms (including a `#tag` next to ordinary text) combine with an **implicit AND** — both must match.
   - **AND / OR / NOT** act as operators when unquoted, and as **ordinary search text when quoted** (e.g. `"rock and roll"`).
   - Story 4 scenarios 3 & 5, and **FR-014** updated.

Note formatting (bold/italic/lists/links) and the Netscape HTML import/export format remain as you approved.

---

You said you'd be happy to approve once these were in. **If you confirm approval, this passes the spec gate and I'll move to the plan gate (`speckit-plan`)** — where I'll present the implementation plan for your review before any code is written.

## 📐 Implementation Plan: Bookmark Manager

**Location:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/` — `plan.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/api.md`, `quickstart.md`

### Proposed technical approach
| Concern | Decision |
|---|---|
| **Shape** | One Node.js app (Express) serving a JSON API **and** a dependency-free vanilla-JS single-page UI, on `0.0.0.0:4000` |
| **Storage** | Local **SQLite** file (`better-sqlite3`) + `data/preserved/` for saved page files |
| **Metadata** | Server fetches page, parses `<title>`/description/OpenGraph/favicon, with graceful fallbacks |
| **Duplicates** | Address **normalisation** (host case, trailing slash, tracking params) → canonical key |
| **Search** | **Hand-written parser/evaluator** so the exact rules hold: implicit-AND between adjacent terms incl. `#tag`+word, AND/OR/NOT literal only when quoted, precedence, malformed-query message |
| **Notes** | `contenteditable` toolbar → HTML **sanitised** to an allow-list (bold/italic/lists/links) |
| **Preservation** | Playwright/Chromium (pinned **1.61.0**, shared binaries) → **single self-contained HTML**; PDFs stored as PDF |
| **Internet Archive** | Optional "Save Page Now" submission, graceful degradation |
| **Import/export** | Netscape bookmark HTML, preserving titles/TAGS/ADD_DATE |
| **Testing** | `node:test` units for grammar/normalise/netscape/metadata + a Playwright smoke test |

### Key design docs
- **data-model.md** — `bookmark`, `tag`, `bookmark_tag`, `saved_search`, `preferences`; independent `is_unread`/`is_archived` flags (new bookmarks read-by-default); bulk tag add/remove as deltas.
- **contracts/api.md** — every endpoint traced to FR numbers, incl. the bulk endpoint's "ids **or** current-match set" and add/remove-tag delta semantics.
- **quickstart.md** — 12 validation scenarios mapped to the user stories.

### Constitution gate
The project constitution is an **unratified template** (all placeholders empty), so there are no ratified gates to enforce — recorded as **PASS** in plan.md. Re-checked after design: still PASS.

### One thing worth your eye
For local page preservation I chose **inlined self-contained HTML via the already-installed Playwright/Chromium** rather than external tools like `monolith` (not guaranteed present). This matches your "self-contained HTML file" requirement and avoids downloading a second browser.

---

**Next step:** review the plan.

- ✅ Approve → I run **`speckit-tasks`** to generate the dependency-ordered task breakdown (another gate before implementation).
- ✏️ Change anything (tech choices, storage, scope of testing) → I'll revise the plan first.

No code will be written until both the plan and tasks are approved.

This plan covers the behaviour I approved, including the corrected search, read-later, bulk-tag, and preservation rules. The proposed local storage and self-contained page-saving approach sound appropriate. I approve the plan; please proceed to the task-breakdown gate.

| Phase | Task count |
|---|---|
| 1 Setup | 3 |

### Suggested MVP scope
**Phases 1–5 (US1–US3, all P1):** save with metadata → no duplicates → browse/sort/open. That's a demoable, independently testable product on its own.

### Tests included (as the spec's testing approach requested)
Targeted unit tests for the highest-risk logic — **search grammar** (T023), **address normalisation** (T008), **duplicate detection** (T017), **metadata parsing** (T012), **Netscape import/export** (T043), **bulk-tag deltas** (T037) — plus one **Playwright smoke test** (T052). Not broad per-endpoint coverage.

### Parallel opportunities
Flagged with `[P]` where files don't collide — e.g. each service vs. its own test file (metadata/search/netscape), and `preserve.js` vs `archiveOrg.js`. Cross-story dependencies are documented so stories stay independently testable.

Every task uses the required checklist format (`- [ ] TID [P?] [US?] description + file path`) and traces to FR numbers and acceptance scenarios.

## ✅ Implementation complete — Bookmark Manager

All **15 phases / 56 tasks** are implemented, marked `[x]` in `tasks.md`, and validated. This cycle delivered **all 12 approved user stories**, not just the MVP, as you requested.

### What was built
A single-user, browser-based bookmark manager (Node + Express, vanilla-JS SPA, local SQLite), serving on `0.0.0.0:4000`:

| Story | Delivered & verified |
|---|---|
| US1 Save + auto-metadata | title/description/icon/preview fetched; editable before & after; invalid URLs → 422 |
| US2 No duplicates | re-saving a variant (host case / trailing slash / tracking params) opens the existing bookmark |
| US3 Browse/sort/open | list shows title/description/tags/icon; sort by date/title; opens original; empty state |
| US4 Search | case-insensitive; `#tag`; quoted phrases; **implicit AND**; **AND/OR/NOT literal only when quoted**; precedence; malformed → 400 |
| US5 Rich edit + notes | edit all fields; sanitised formatted notes (scripts stripped); tag suggestions; edit-to-collide blocked |
| US6 Read-later | ordinary by default; unread only when chosen; dedicated unread view |
| US7 Archive/delete | archive hides from list+search, restorable; delete needs confirmation |
| US8 Bulk actions | selection **or** "all matching"; tag add/remove **as deltas** (other tags preserved); partial-failure reporting |
| US9 Saved searches | named query + included/excluded tags; apply/rename/delete |
| US10 Import/export | Netscape format, titles/tags/dates preserved; dedup on import; invalid file → 422 |
| US11 Preservation | **self-contained HTML** (scripts stripped) via Chromium; **PDFs kept as PDF**; optional Internet Archive with graceful failure |
| US12 Preferences | default sort, items per view, text size — persisted and applied |

### Testing (`npm test` → exit 0)
- **23 unit** tests (search grammar, normalisation, metadata, Netscape)
- **13 DB-integration** tests (CRUD, duplicates, archive, bulk-tag deltas, saved searches)
- **2 Playwright smoke** tests (loads + harness-ready; save→list)

### Notable engineering decisions (recorded in the plan/research docs)
- **Storage switched from `better-sqlite3` to Node's built-in `node:sqlite`.** The native addon crashed at startup ~80% of the time on this Node 24 build; the built-in module is API-compatible for our use and starts **5/5 reliably**. This is an internal-only change — no spec or behaviour impact.

### Ready for review
- `.harness/app.json` declares `npm start` on port 4000; the port is free so the broker will start a fresh instance (showing the friendly empty state, `data-harness-ready`).
- Reference screenshot saved at `prototypes/bookmark-manager-main.png`.

The application is ready for your acceptance at `http://maker:4000`. You can save a URL live and exercise search, tags, read-later, archive, bulk actions, saved searches, import/export, and page preservation.

The completed application and verification report match the behaviour I approved across all 12 stories. The storage change is fine since it does not affect how the app works for me. I accept this implementation.
